description: Implement a language-agnostic mutation testing framework using TDD.

tasks.title: Validate mutation plan against schema
tasks.description: A function validates a mutation plan against its schema.
acceptance_criteria: A valid mutation plan passes validation (exit 0).
An invalid mutation plan (e.g., missing required field) fails validation (exit non-zero).

tasks.title: Apply a single mutation to a source file
tasks.description: A function applies a single mutation from a plan to a source file.
acceptance_criteria: Applying a mutation replaces the target text in the source file.
The original source file remains unchanged after mutation.

tasks.title: Respect mutation location fields (start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col)
tasks.description: When the same original text appears multiple times — the mutation should only be applied at the exact location indicated by start_row, end_row, start_col, end_col.
acceptance_criteria: A mutation whose original text appears multiple times in the source file is only applied at the specified row/col location, not at other occurrences.
A mutation whose original text does NOT match the text at the specified row/col location reports an error (the mismatch indicates the mutation candidate is stale or the source has changed).
The replacement text is inserted at the correct column boundary within the specified row, replacing exactly the range [start_col, end_col).

tasks.title: Run a test command and report mutant outcome
tasks.description: A function executes a test command, prints whether the mutant was killed or survived, and indicates the outcome.
acceptance_criteria: When the test command exits with 0 (all tests pass), the function prints 👾 survived and returns false.
When the test command exits non-zero (at least one test fails), the function prints 🏹 killed and returns true.

tasks.title: Orchestrate the mutation testing loop
tasks.description: The orchestrator reads a mutation plan from a JSON file, applies each mutation one at a time to the original source file (in place), runs the test command after each, prints per-mutation outcome, and writes a final JSON report with killed/survived results.
acceptance_criteria: Given a mutation plan JSON file and a test command, the orchestrator applies each mutation individually to the source file (in place), runs the test command, and prints 🏹 killed or 👾 survived for each mutation.
Each mutation is applied to the original source — not to the result of a previous mutation. The source is reverted between mutations.
A JSON report entry is written as each mutation is processed, containing the original mutation record with an additional killed field.
Entries are appended incrementally, so a partial report is available if processing stops early.
The killed value is true when the test command exits non-zero (the mutation was killed) and false when it exits zero (the mutation survived).
The report file is valid JSON matching the mutation record structure except for the added killed field.
After the orchestrator completes, the source files are restored to their original state.
